description:
FILED s457aj (Opus agent AJ, round 14).  PRE-EXISTING; newly REACHABLE because
#850 un-dropped t/io/open.t's line 267, so the file now runs past line 362.

t/io/open.t:362:

    eval { open $99, "foo" };
    like($@, qr/Modification of a read-only value attempted/, 'readonly fh');

perl: `$99` is a regex capture variable, which is read-only, so `open` fails
at run time with "Modification of a read-only value attempted" -- trappable,
which is what the row asserts.

PCL: `$99` is emitted as an ordinary (never-declared) variable reference, so
the file carries an unbound-variable diagnostic -- the companion runner
records it as this file's `sig`, `unbound:$99` -- and row 140 fails because
`$@` does not carry perl's message.

THE FAMILY: `$1`..`$N` are read-only in perl and PCL treats a HIGH-numbered
one (past any group the file's patterns define) as an ordinary global.  Two
halves, and the second is the useful one:
  (a) a capture variable that no pattern in the file defines still READS as
      undef, which is right;
  (b) it must not be WRITABLE -- `open $99, â¦`, `$1 = 5`, `chop $1` are all
      "Modification of a read-only value attempted" in perl.
Probe (a) and (b) separately before deciding the layer: (b) is a box-level
read-only flag on the capture cells, which is runtime, not parser.

BAR: t/io/open.t row 140 ("readonly fh"), and the `sig` column for that file
returns to empty.  A `cl/` change makes the sweep non-optional.
subject: A CAPTURE variable used as a filehandle (`eval { open $99, "foo" }`) is a read-only error in perl; PCL emits an unbound reference
